name: Al-Falaq
meaning: The Daybreak, The Dawn, or The Splitting
revelation_details: Madinan (While some classical scholars debate this, the strongest authentic traditions indicate it was revealed in Madinah alongside Surah An-Nas, specifically in response to a physical and spiritual attack on the Prophet).
core_theme: This Surah is the ultimate shield against external evils. It teaches the believer to actively seek refuge in the Lord of the Dawn from the hidden, terrifying things in the outside world that we cannot control - including the darkness of the night, black magic, and the toxic, destructive power of human envy.
name_origin:
The Surah gets its name from the final word of the first verse: Al-Falaq. The word Falaq comes from a root meaning to split or tear open. It refers perfectly to the dawn or daybreak, because the morning light "splits" the heavy darkness of the night.

The Mu'awwidhatayn (The Two Surahs of Refuge): Before diving into the verses, it is essential to understand that Surah Al-Falaq and the final chapter, Surah An-Nas, are a matching pair. They were revealed together and are collectively known as the Mu'awwidhatayn (The Two Protectors/The Two Surahs of Refuge). The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) deeply loved these two Surahs. He used to seek refuge in Allah from the evil eye of humans and jinn using various prayers, but according to an authentic Hadith (Sunan at-Tirmidhi), when the Mu'awwidhatayn were revealed, he dropped the other prayers and only used these two Surahs for protection.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Ultimate Refuge from External Evils

points.label: The Command to Seek Refuge
points.detail: Allah commands the Prophet and all believers to say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak." (This establishes that ultimate safety only comes from the Creator of the dawn).

points.label: General Protection
points.detail: From the evil of that which He created." (A sweeping request for protection against any harm that might come from animals, humans, insects, or environmental dangers).

points.label: Protection from the Night
points.detail: And from the evil of darkness when it settles." (The night is specifically mentioned because when darkness falls, human vision is limited, predators hunt, and hidden dangers or criminals emerge).

points.label: Protection from Sorcery
points.detail: And from the evil of the blowers in knots." (This specifically targets black magic and sorcery. In ancient times, magicians would tie knots and blow on them to cast malicious spells).

points.label: Protection from Envy
points.detail: And from the evil of an envier when he envies." (This asks for safety against the "evil eye" and the destructive jealousy of people who wish to see your blessings destroyed).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Surah Al-Falaq is a powerful chapter of protection, teaching the believer how to seek safety with the Creator against the physical and hidden harms that exist in the outside world.
• The Command to Seek Refuge: Allah commands the Prophet and all believers to say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak." (This establishes that ultimate safety only comes from the Creator of the dawn).
• General Protection: "From the evil of that which He created." (A sweeping request for protection against any harm that might come from animals, humans, insects, or environmental dangers).
• Protection from the Night: "And from the evil of darkness when it settles." (The night is specifically mentioned because when darkness falls, human vision is limited, predators hunt, and hidden dangers or criminals emerge).
• Protection from Sorcery: "And from the evil of the blowers in knots." (This specifically targets black magic and sorcery. In ancient times, magicians would tie knots and blow on them to cast malicious spells).
• Protection from Envy: "And from the evil of an envier when he envies." (This asks for safety against the "evil eye" and the destructive jealousy of people who wish to see your blessings destroyed).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
Classical scholars of Tafsir, such as Ibn Al-Qayyim and As-Sa'di, provide a fascinating psychological and spiritual breakdown of this Surah. They explain that Surah Al-Falaq is dedicated entirely to protecting a person from external evils - things that happen to you from the outside world, which are largely out of your control.
The choice of the word "Daybreak" is incredibly symbolic. When a person is surrounded by the darkness of the night, the fear of magic, or the secret jealousy of an envier, they often feel trapped in a dark, helpless situation. By asking the "Lord of the Daybreak" for help, the believer remembers that just as God effortlessly splits the darkness of the night to bring forth the bright morning light, He can easily split through any dark magic, plot, or calamity to bring safety and relief.
Furthermore, scholars note that jealousy (envy) is placed at the very end of the Surah. This is because envy is often the root cause of all the other evils mentioned. A person only plots against you in the dark, or resorts to dark magic, because their heart was first corrupted by intense jealousy regarding the blessings God gave you.

stories_in_surah.title: The Historical Story: The Spell on the Prophet
stories_in_surah.content:
To understand the intense need for this "shield," we must look at the specific, authentic historical event (recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari) that prompted their revelation.

In Madinah, a man named Labid ibn al-A'sam, who was secretly a hypocrite and practiced dark magic, was hired by the enemies of Islam to put a severe curse on the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Labid managed to get hold of some hair from the Prophet's comb and used it to cast a dark, debilitating spell. He tied eleven knots in a string, blowing dark incantations onto each knot, and hid it at the bottom of a deep, unused well under a heavy rock.

The Prophet (pbuh) began to suffer terribly. He became physically weak, deeply confused, and suffered from severe memory lapses (he would think he had done something when he hadn't). This went on for weeks, and the Prophet (pbuh) constantly made intense du'a (supplication) to Allah for healing.

Finally, Allah answered his prayer. He sent two angels to the Prophet (pbuh) in a dream. One sat at his head, the other at his feet, and they revealed exactly what had happened, who cast the spell, and where it was hidden. The Prophet (pbuh) sent his companions to the well. They pulled up the rock and found the string with the eleven knots.

Allah then revealed Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas, which together contain exactly eleven verses. As the Prophet (pbuh) recited each verse, one knot miraculously untied itself. When he finished the final verse, the last knot broke, and the Prophet (pbuh) stood up feeling completely cured, as if he had just been untied from a heavy rope.

deep_dives.title: Seeking the Lord of the Dawn (Verses 1-2)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah begins with a direct, powerful command: "Say, 'I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak (Al-Falaq).'"

Why does Allah tell us to seek refuge specifically in the "Lord of the Dawn"? Think about the psychology of the night. When you are alone in the dark, fears are amplified. Every shadow looks like a monster, and every sound is terrifying. You feel helpless. But the moment the sun breaks over the horizon (the dawn), all those shadows disappear, and relief washes over you. Allah is telling us: No matter how dark, terrifying, or inescapable your situation feels, I am the Lord who splits the darkness to bring the morning light. I can easily split your darkness and bring you relief.

Then, Allah defines the first, broad category of evil we are seeking protection from: "From the evil of that which He created." This is a comprehensive blanket statement. It covers absolutely every harmful thing in existence - predatory animals, diseases, toxic people, accidents, and unseen forces. We ask the Creator to protect us from the harm inherent in His creation.

deep_dives.title: The Three Hidden Evils (Verses 3-4)
deep_dives.content:
After the general request for protection, Allah zeroes in on three very specific, highly dangerous, and hidden evils that human beings cannot fight with physical weapons.

1. The Darkness of the Night: "And from the evil of darkness when it settles." When the sun goes down, crime rates go up. Wild animals come out to hunt. People who want to do harm hide in the shadows. Most terrifyingly, the unseen forces (like evil jinn and magic) are most active at night. We are physically most vulnerable when we are asleep in the dark, so we ask God to be our night watchman.

2. The Practitioners of Dark Magic: "And from the evil of the blowers in knots." This directly addresses the historical event of Labid's curse, but it applies to all forms of black magic (Sihr). In ancient times (and still today in some cultures), witches and sorcerers would tie knots in a string or cloth, blowing their cursed breath and evil incantations onto them to cause harm, illness, or separation between husbands and wives. We cannot see magic, and we cannot punch a curse, so we must seek refuge in the only Power that can neutralize it.

deep_dives.title: The Toxicity of Envy (Verse 5)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah concludes with one of the most common, toxic, and destructive forces in human society:

"And from the evil of an envier when he envies."

Hasad (Envy/Jealousy) is a terrifying spiritual disease. It is not just wishing you had what someone else has (which is normal). True Hasad is seeing a blessing Allah gave to someone else - a good job, a beautiful family, health, or a nice home - and actively hating them for it, wishing for that blessing to be completely destroyed.

The Danger of the Evil Eye: Envy is dangerous because it often leads to action (like slander, backbiting, or trying to ruin someone's reputation). But even more terrifyingly, the Prophet (pbuh) confirmed that the "Evil Eye" (Al-'Ayn) is a reality. When a person looks at you with intense, hateful jealousy, that dark spiritual energy can actually cause physical harm, illness, or loss of your blessing.

You cannot always tell who is envious of you. They might smile to your face while hating you in their heart. Because this evil is completely hidden inside someone else's chest, you have no defense against it except to wrap yourself in the unbreakable armor of the Lord of the Dawn.
